solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plant a tree containing minimum of leaves

indicators.note: containing says the pair of pieces before it holds another letter between them

parts.note: a pine is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is taken here as its smallest part, its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a tree that bears only a few leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a small plant native to mountain heights, grown in rock gardens.

clue.text: New Scottish party — at heart it's something fishy!

parts.note: Alba is the Scottish nationalist party founded by Alex Salmond in 2021
the heart of something is its core

explanation.surface: A political commentator suspects the new Scottish party of being shady at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests something suspect, but it points to a real fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned tuna, so literally a creature of the sea.

clue.text: Having a mate? Some requirement that's right within

parts.note: some of a thing is a part of it

indicators.note: within says the letter for right sits inside the word for requirement

parts.note: a requirement is a need

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether having a companion is partly a necessity that ought to be a right.
explanation.definitionFit: To be partnered is to be paired off with a companion or spouse.

clue.text: Revolutionary socialist academic who shows agreement?

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the pieces are read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A left-wing lecturer is described, then asked whether he merely goes along with things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the tail 'who shows agreement', read as 'one who shows agreement'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who nods the head signals assent, so is a person giving agreement.

clue.text: Jubilant church suffering setback and not going anywhere

indicators.note: suffering a setback means being sent back, so the church letters are reversed

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
static means stationary, not moving

explanation.surface: A church is joyful despite a setback and having stalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Jubilant and the answer both describe being overjoyed, rapturously happy.

clue.text: Cop a noble man, I fancy — easy to get along with

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, and an imagined version of these words is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: A speaker catches an aristocrat for a policeman and finds him friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable, friendly person is good company and easy to be around.

clue.text: Get restless, somewhat lacking support

indicators.note: somewhat lacking says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone grows fidgety for want of support.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of legs and a crossbar used to hold up a table top.

clue.text: Make gentle progress with hospital pledge

parts.note: to trot is to move along at an easy pace
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient recovers slowly with a hospital's promise of care.
explanation.definitionFit: A troth is an old word for a solemn promise, as in plighting one's troth at a wedding.

clue.text: What may be said to go with a snap

definitions.text: What may be said to go with a snap

parts.words: What may be said to go with a snap
parts.note: photographers tell sitters to say this word to make them smile for a snap, and it also goes with a snack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' reads as a quick meal, but it is a photograph, posed for by saying the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this dairy word for a camera stretches the mouth into a smile.

clue.text: Disaffected directors, from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear signals a word that sounds like the one spoken

parts.note: a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that the company directors are discontented.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weary and uninterested has lost enthusiasm, a mild kind of disaffection.

clue.text: Top guy getting miners drunk on beer

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

indicators.note: drunk suggests the words on beer are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A boss gets the colliery workers intoxicated on beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The person at the head of an organisation is its leader, the boss.

clue.text: Upset soon clear, upset over social function? It may suggest event has been boycotted

definitions.text: It may suggest event has been boycotted

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for soon is read backwards

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: the second upset turns the word for clear upside down as well

parts.note: nett means clear, as in clear profit after deductions
a dance is a social function

explanation.surface: Someone confusingly says a function was upset and cleared, wondering whether it was shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the reversed pieces above DANCE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to turn up is what a boycott produces: people staying away from the event.

clue.text: Business as against research establishment

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: Commerce is set in opposition to a scientific institute.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a firm or company, so the word can mean a business.

clue.text: Characters beginning and ending in Harwich

definitions.text: Characters beginning and ending in Harwich

parts.words: Characters beginning and ending in Harwich
parts.note: the town name Harwich opens and closes with the same letter, and these are its spoken names

explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people in the Essex port; they are letters, the ones at each end of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The written-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, in the plural, names a pair of letters.

clue.text: Vessel taking soldiers back repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the reversed piece appears twice in a row
taking back means reading the letters for soldiers backwards

parts.note: OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A ship ferries troops home again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-on roll-off ferry is a ship that vehicles drive straight onto and off.

clue.text: Vociferous leader of socialists against nuclear weapon

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Trident is the UK's submarine-launched nuclear missile system

explanation.surface: A left-wing leader loudly opposes nuclear arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and harsh in protest describes someone clamorous and vociferous.

clue.text: Squire out travelling around in a shade of blue

indicators.note: letters travelling move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A country gentleman out on a journey is wrapped in blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The gemstone name also names a greenish-blue colour.

clue.text: Drunken male not minimally healthy? Not if he drinks this!

indicators.note: drunken suggests letters staggering into a new order
minimally means taking just the smallest part, the first letter

explanation.surface: A drunk man is far from healthy, and won't be if he drinks this.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether the drunk is healthy; the answer is wood alcohol, a poison, so 'Not if he drinks this' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood alcohol is toxic, causing blindness or death, so drinking it ruins health.

clue.text: No sun, egad, not a shimmer in these places!

indicators.note: not says the letter a is left out of the pool before rearranging
a shimmer is a wavering, so the letters shift into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that underground cells get no sun and not even a glimmer of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground prison cells are the dark places with no sunlight.

clue.text: Token number — least possible — I'm not included

indicators.note: not included says the letters of I'm are left out of the word before

parts.note: minimal means the least possible

explanation.surface: Someone describes a token amount as a tiny figure that leaves them out.
explanation.definitionFit: A token payment is one in name only, very small and not real value.

clue.text: French brother runs away, having escaped?

indicators.note: runs away means the letter for runs goes from the word

parts.note: frère is French for brother
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A French monk flees, and someone wonders if he got out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has escaped is at liberty, no longer held.

clue.text: At far end of pub spot actress

indicators.note: at the far end of says the spot comes after the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: A film star is spotted at the far end of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigitte Bardot is the French film star of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Reprimand in female gym — it's very cold

indicators.note: in says the reprimand sits inside the letters for female and gym

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym lessons
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A telling-off in a women's gym leaves things chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Frappé describes drinks that are iced or chilled, served over shaved ice.

clue.text: Horrified member hugged by Jones the singer?

indicators.note: hugged by says the limb sits inside the singer's name

parts.note: Aled Jones is the Welsh singer, famous as a choirboy
an arm is a member, a limb

explanation.surface: A Welsh singer embraces a fan who is shocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frightened or dismayed means being in a state of fear or shock.

clue.text: Hidden persuader brought on board by bad manager

indicators.note: brought on board means carried within, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A poor boss recruits a secret influencer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Hidden Persuaders' is Vance Packard's book about advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising people subtly persuade the public to buy, hence the phrase from Packard's book.

clue.text: Such may have been rotten old boy turning crude

indicators.note: turning means the letters for old boy are turned round

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
rough means crude, unrefined

explanation.surface: A former pupil has gone bad and become coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten boroughs were tiny pre-1832 British constituencies that still elected MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: A town returning a member to Parliament with very few voters was called rotten.

clue.text: I condemn a misdirected authority

indicators.note: misdirected letters are sent the wrong way, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denounces power that has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Control or power over others is the meaning shared by both words.

clue.text: Risk to health in jail — closed-in society unwanted

indicators.note: unwanted says the society letter is thrown out of the word for jail

parts.note: a jail is a prison
S abbreviates society, and here it is the letter shut inside the word for jail

explanation.surface: Health hazards in prison come from a closed community no one wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfolded protein that causes diseases such as CJD is a hazard to health.

clue.text: Altering? Altering that more complex?

indicators.note: the second altering tells the solver to change the order of the letters of the first

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether changing something will make it more complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more knotted or intricate is more complicated, the comparative of knotty.

clue.text: Cancel another performance by learner with time running out

indicators.note: by says the learner letter comes in beside the rest
time running out means the letter for time leaves

parts.note: a repeat is another showing or performance
L is the learner sign on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A show's rerun is axed because a novice took too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a law or order is to cancel it officially.
